# 1. Purpose and scope
This specification defines the V10 menu that replaces the current Shahi menu. It turns the analysis in the source workbook into build instructions for the Development team and roll-out instructions for the Implementation team.
The scope covers every row of the 11 module sheets in the workbook (Product, Sales, Sourcing, Production, Inventory, QC, FA, Planning, TNA, Reports, Admin), together with the To Confirm and Excel Data Errors sheets. Screen behaviour inside each page is out of scope unless stated; this document is about where each screen sits in the menu, what it is called, how it is reached and who can see it.

## 1.1 How to read this document
• Section 2 summarises the gap between the legacy menu and the V10 HTML mock.
• Section 3 sets the naming and structure rules every menu entry must follow.
• Section 4 lists the corrections already applied to the Proposed Menu column.
• Section 5 is the target V10 menu, module by module. This is the build list.
• Sections 6 and 7 are the Development and Implementation requirements.
• Section 8 lists open decisions. Appendix A maps every legacy menu row to its V10 location.

## 1.2 Terms

[TABLE 2: Table 2 · 9 rows · columns: Term (text), Meaning (text) · identifiers: Term]
| Term | Meaning |
| Legacy menu | The menu currently on the Shahi server (columns A–E of each module sheet). |
| Proposed Menu / V10 path | Column J. Full navigation path in the new menu, written Module > Sub Menu > Page Name. |
| Page Name | Column K. The label shown on the final menu item and as the page title. |
| Existing | The V10 path already exists in the V10 menu (Proposal Basis = "In V10 menu"). |
| New | The V10 path does not exist yet and must be added (Proposal Basis = "Proposed: new under …"). |
| Confirm | Closest V10 match chosen; the Product Owner must confirm before build (Proposal Basis = "Closest V10 menu - confirm"). |
| Menu group | A V10 path that has other V10 paths below it. It opens a sub-menu and does not open a page. |
| Folder (review) | A legacy folder that, after the 3-level rule, has no pages left beneath it. Dev must remove it or turn it into a landing page (see 8.3). |
| Technology | Column I. The platform of the legacy page: 1.0, 4.0 or Angular. "Not found" means the page was not found on the Shahi server. |

# 2. Current state summary
The legacy Excel menu holds 635 menu items in 11 modules. The V10 HTML mock holds 252 menu items in 13 modules. Matching was done by meaning, because V10 renames and regroups many menus (for example Buyer becomes Customer, Production becomes Manufacturing and QC becomes Quality & Compliance).

Note: the module rows add up to 639 while the Summary sheet states 635 legacy items; the Summary sheet itself flags this as a mismatch. It does not affect the build list in Section 5, which is generated row by row.

## 2.1 Key findings that drive the work
• Finance is the largest gap. Seven whole sections have no V10 menu (General Ledger, Inter Company, Taxation & Compliances, Inventory Financials, Fixed Assets, Migrations, GST Doc Integration). Most of the new V10 entries in this specification are in Finance Management.
• Setup masters are the next gap. Many Sales, Product and Sourcing codes are not in the V10 mock and are proposed as new entries under the relevant Setups sub-menu.
• Several transaction screens are missing from V10, including Process Definition, Good Transfer Note, Alteration / Additional Process, Liability Management, Chargebacks, Supplier Block Booking, Advance License, Sample Value Confirmation, Return-to-Processor and Return-to-Supplier dispatch, OC to OC Roll Transfer and Update Pallet Location.
• V10 adds 86 menus that Shahi does not have today (for example Supplier Onboarding, Audits, Recipes, Batch Traceability, Security & Access, Workflow & Approvals). Seven of them are marked "Removed in V10" and are excluded.
• Many legacy menu rows are actions, not screens. Legacy entries named New, List, Search or Pending normally become buttons or tabs inside the parent page (see 6.3).

# 3. Menu standards
Every entry in the V10 menu must follow these rules. They were applied to the Proposed Menu column and are the acceptance rules for any later change.
• Three levels at most. A path is Module > Sub Menu > Page Name. Where the legacy structure was deeper, the levels in between are dropped and the page sits directly under the sub-menu.
• The page name is the last level of the path. Column K must always equal the last part of column J. The page title shown on screen must use the same text.
• List menus use the plural. A page that lists records is named in the plural (Suppliers, Seasons, Themes, Production Orders, PO Templates). Where the legacy name is plural, the V10 name must not be singular.
• Separator format. Levels are separated by space, greater-than sign, space (" > "). No empty levels, no double spaces, no missing spaces.
• Title case. Every word in a menu label starts with a capital letter except short joining words (of, for, to, and). Example: Payment Terms, not Payment terms.
• One path, one page. Two different screens must not share the same full path. Where they do, one must be renamed (see 8.2).
• Actions are not menu items. New, List, Search, Pending and similar entries become buttons or tabs inside the page and are controlled by action-level permissions.
• No test, personal or note rows. Rows such as "Yudesh Sir" or requirement notes typed as menu rows must not be built.

# 4. Corrections already applied to the Proposed Menu
The following corrections were made to columns J and K of the source workbook before this specification was produced. Dev should build from the corrected workbook, not from earlier copies.

| Sales | 13, 20, 22 | Missing space or double space after ">" | Single " > " separator | Format (rule 4) |

## 4.2 Three-level rule
153 rows had paths deeper than three levels. Each was shortened to Module > Sub Menu > Page Name by dropping the levels in between. For example, Inventory > Issue and Dispatches > List > Instructions > Common GDI For FPPO became Inventory > Issue and Dispatches > Common GDI For FPPO. The Proposal Basis notes for Inventory rows 18–27 were updated to match.

# 5. Target V10 menu (build list)
The build list below has one row per distinct V10 path. Several legacy rows can point to the same V10 path; they are listed together in the last column. In total there are 533 distinct V10 paths: 439 pages, 46 menu groups and 48 folders to review. By status, 216 already exist in V10, 310 are new and 7 need confirmation.

# 6. Development specification

## 6.1 Menu configuration record
Each row of the Section 5 build list becomes one menu configuration record. The record must hold the fields below. Fields marked "from workbook" are filled directly from the source workbook; the rest are set by Dev.

[TABLE 19: Table 19 · 11 rows · columns: Field (text), Description (text), Source (text) · identifiers: Field]
| Field | Description | Source |
| Menu ID | Unique, stable key. Proposed format MODULE.SUBMENU.PAGE in upper case with spaces removed (for example SOURCING.SETUPS.SUPPLIERS). | Dev |
| Level 1 – Module | First part of the V10 path. | From workbook (col J) |
| Level 2 – Sub Menu | Second part of the V10 path. Not clickable; opens the sub-menu. | From workbook (col J) |
| Level 3 – Page Name | Third part of the V10 path; also the page title and breadcrumb label. | From workbook (col K) |
| Node type | Menu group, Page or Folder (review). | Section 5 |
| Technology | 1.0, 4.0 or Angular; decides how the page is opened (6.4). | From workbook (col I) |
| Target URL / route | Route of the existing legacy page, or of the new V10 page. | Dev |
| Legacy menu IDs | All legacy menu entries merged into this page; used for rights migration and redirects. | Appendix A |
| Sort order | Order within the sub-menu. Default: as in the V10 HTML mock; new items placed after existing ones alphabetically unless the Product Owner says otherwise. | Dev / PO |
| Actions | List of in-page actions (New, List, Search, Pending, Approve …) with their own permission keys. | Legacy child rows |
| Status | Existing, New or Confirm. | Section 5 |

## 6.2 Navigation behaviour
• The menu must never show more than three levels. A Level 2 item opens its list of pages; it does not open a page itself.
• The breadcrumb on every page reads Module > Sub Menu > Page Name, using exactly the text in the build list.
• The browser tab title and the page heading use the Page Name.
• A V10 path that appears under more than one legacy module (for example Reporting, or Sales > Setups > Payment Terms reached from Sourcing and Finance) is built once and shown once.
• Menu search, where available, must index the Page Name and the legacy names in the Legacy menu IDs field, so users can still find a page by its old name during the transition.

## 6.3 Actions inside pages
Legacy rows named New, List, Search, Pending and similar have been mapped to the same V10 path as their parent. Dev must not create these as menu items. Instead:
• List and Search become the default view of the page (a list with search/filter).
• New becomes a button on the list view that opens the entry form.
• Other children with their own screen (for example Supplier Invoice Return List, Download Invoices, Update GL Date) keep their own V10 path as shown in Section 5.
• Each action has its own permission key under the page Menu ID (for example FINANCE.AP.SUPPLIERINVOICE.NEW), so that rights held on the legacy New or List entries can be carried over exactly.

## 6.4 Technology handling
The build list carries the legacy technology for each page. The menu must open the page in the correct way for that technology.

[TABLE 20: Table 20 · 6 rows · columns: Technology (text), Pages (distinct V10 paths) (integer), Requirement (text) · identifiers: Technology]
| Technology | Pages (distinct V10 paths) | Requirement |
| 4.0 | 220 | Open the existing 4.0 route. Check that the page title and breadcrumb take the V10 Page Name, not the old label. |
| 1.0 | 87 | Open the existing 1.0 page inside the V10 shell. Confirm that 1.0 pages can show the V10 breadcrumb; if not, list them as a known limitation. |
| Angular | 75 | Open the existing Angular route. Same title and breadcrumb check as 4.0. |
| Mixed (e.g. "1.0, Angular") | 18 | Several legacy pages on different technologies merge into one V10 page. Dev must choose the single page that the V10 entry opens and turn the others into actions or remove them. Record the decision in the Target URL field. |
| Not found | 10 | The legacy page was not found on the Shahi server. Dev to confirm whether the page exists before linking it. |
| HTML only | 77 | Exists only in the V10 HTML mock. Treat as new V10 functionality; build or hide according to the product release plan. |

## 6.5 New menu entries
310 V10 paths are new. For each one Dev must create the menu record, link it to the existing legacy page (most new entries are existing Shahi screens that the V10 mock does not show yet) and apply the standards in Section 3. The largest blocks are Finance Management (141), Sales (30), Sourcing (25) and Products (23).

## 6.6 Legacy links and redirects
• Saved bookmarks, dashboard tiles, e-mail links and notifications that point to a legacy menu must keep working. Each legacy menu ID in Appendix A redirects to its V10 page.
• Where a legacy entry has become an action (New, List), the redirect opens the V10 page with that action selected.
• Legacy entries excluded from V10 (Section 8.4) redirect to the module home page with a short message.

## 6.7 Permissions
• A user sees a Page only if they hold its view permission. A Menu group is shown only if the user can see at least one page under it. An empty module is hidden.
• Rights migrate from legacy menu IDs to V10 Menu IDs using Appendix A. Where several legacy entries merge into one V10 page, the user gets the page if they had any of the legacy entries; action rights are carried per action.
• Dev must produce a migration report listing every user and role whose visible menu changes, for Implementation to review (7.1).

## 6.8 Acceptance criteria
• Every Page in Section 5 can be reached in no more than three clicks from the main menu.
• No menu path has more than three levels and no two pages share a path.
• Menu label, page title and breadcrumb match the build list exactly, including plural and capitalisation.
• No New, List or Search entries appear as menu items; they are available as actions with working permissions.
• Every legacy menu ID in Appendix A opens the correct V10 page.
• A user migrated from a legacy role sees the same set of screens and actions as before, apart from changes approved in Section 8.
• All items marked Confirm or Folder (review) have a recorded decision before release.

# 7. Implementation specification

## 7.1 Roles and rights migration
• Export the current Shahi roles, users and their menu rights before the change.
• Run the Dev migration (6.7) on a copy of production data.
• Compare the before and after menu for each role using the Dev migration report. Investigate every role that loses or gains a screen.
• Pay special attention to merged pages (Appendix A rows that share a V10 path) and to the Finance module, where most entries are new.
• Get sign-off on the final role matrix from the customer process owners for each module.

## 7.2 User communication
• Publish a "Where did my menu go?" guide built from Appendix A, one page per legacy module, sorted by legacy menu name.
• Explain the three main changes: menus renamed (for example Buyer to Customer), menus moved between modules (for example Sales ASN to Logistic, Material Requisitions to Sourcing), and New/List entries now being buttons inside the page.
• Communicate module renames: Product → Products and Development, Production → Manufacturing, QC → Quality & Compliance, FA → Finance Management, Planning → Plan, TNA → Utilities > TNA, Admin → Administrators and Utilities.

## 7.3 Training

[TABLE 21: Table 21 · 6 rows · columns: Audience (text), Focus (text), Priority (text) · identifiers: Audience]
| Audience | Focus | Priority |
| Finance users | Large number of new entries; new sub-menus Commercial Management, Tax Management, Asset Management, Intercompany & Branch Accounting, Finance Setup & Configuration. | High |
| Sales and merchandising | Customers Management, Sales Order, Enquiry & Projection; sampling moved to Development; ASN and shipping moved to Logistic. | High |
| Sourcing and logistics | Supplier Management under Setups; Indent; inbound shipments and forward booking under Logistic. | High |
| Stores / inventory | Receipts and Issue and Dispatches sub-menus; Material Requisitions moved to Sourcing. | Medium |
| Production, QC, Planning | Module renames and new Setups entries. | Medium |
| Administrators | Business Configuration, Enterprise Structure and Integration under Utilities. | Medium |

## 7.4 User acceptance testing
• For each module, a key user opens every Page in Section 5 from the menu and confirms the right screen opens.
• Test at least one legacy bookmark or link per module and confirm the redirect.
• Test New, List and Search actions on merged pages with a user who had only one of the legacy rights.
• Confirm role visibility for at least one user per role in the migration report.
• Record defects against the Menu ID so Dev can trace them to the build list.

## 7.5 Cut-over and rollback
• Freeze menu and role changes in Shahi from the agreed date until go-live.
• Deploy the V10 menu configuration and run the rights migration in the agreed downtime window.
• Smoke-test one page per module with a key user before releasing to all users.
• Keep the legacy menu configuration and role export so the previous menu can be restored if a blocking defect is found.
• Provide floor support for the first week, with the Appendix A guide at hand.

CANDIDATES FOR REVIEW (possible definitions, formulas, validations, steps; not confirmed knowledge)
- table (starttable 1): Table 1: Item, Detail (8 rows; identifiers: Item)
- definition (§ 1. Purpose and scope): Screen behaviour inside each page is out of scope unless stated; this document is about where each screen sits in the menu, what it is called, how it is reached and who can see it.
- validation (§ 1. Purpose and scope › 1.1 How to read this document): Section 3 sets the naming and structure rules every menu entry must follow.
- definition (§ 1. Purpose and scope › 1.1 How to read this document): Section 5 is the target V10 menu, module by module.
- definition (§ 1. Purpose and scope › 1.1 How to read this document): This is the build list.
- definition (§ 1. Purpose and scope › 1.1 How to read this document): Sections 6 and 7 are the Development and Implementation requirements.
- workflow_steps (§ 1. Purpose and scope › 1.1 How to read this document): 1.1 How to read this document: / 1. Section 2 summarises the gap between the legacy menu and the V10 HTML mock. / 2. Section 3 sets the naming and structure rules every menu entry must follow. / 3. Section 4 lists the corrections already applied to the Proposed Menu column. / 4. Section 5 is the target V10 menu, module by module. This is the build list. / 5. Sections 6 and 7 are the Development and Implementation requirements. / 6. Section 8 lists open decisions. Appendix A maps every legacy menu row to its V10 location.
- table (§ 1. Purpose and scope › 1.2 Terms, table 2): Table 2: Term, Meaning (9 rows; identifiers: Term)
- table (§ 2. Current state summary, table 3): Table 3: Legacy module, V10 module(s), Legacy items, Available in HTML, Sub Menu not Available, Not Available in HTML, Only in HTML (12 rows; identifiers: Legacy module)
- definition (§ 2. Current state summary › 2.1 Key findings that drive the work): Finance is the largest gap.
- definition (§ 2. Current state summary › 2.1 Key findings that drive the work): Most of the new V10 entries in this specification are in Finance Management.
- definition (§ 2. Current state summary › 2.1 Key findings that drive the work): Setup masters are the next gap.
- definition (§ 2. Current state summary › 2.1 Key findings that drive the work): Several transaction screens are missing from V10, including Process Definition, Good Transfer Note, Alteration / Additional Process, Liability Management, Chargebacks, Supplier Block Booking, Advance License, Sample Value Confirmation, Return-to-Processor and Return-to-Supplier dispatch, OC to OC Roll Transfer and Update Pallet Location.
- validation (§ 2. Current state summary › 2.1 Key findings that drive the work): Several transaction screens are missing from V10, including Process Definition, Good Transfer Note, Alteration / Additional Process, Liability Management, Chargebacks, Supplier Block Booking, Advance License, Sample Value Confirmation, Return-to-Processor and Return-to-Supplier dispatch, OC to OC Roll Transfer and Update Pallet Location.
- definition (§ 2. Current state summary › 2.1 Key findings that drive the work): Seven of them are marked "Removed in V10" and are excluded.
- definition (§ 2. Current state summary › 2.1 Key findings that drive the work): Many legacy menu rows are actions, not screens.
- workflow_steps (§ 2. Current state summary › 2.1 Key findings that drive the work): 2.1 Key findings that drive the work: / 1. Finance is the largest gap. Seven whole sections have no V10 menu (General Ledger, Inter Company, Taxation & Compliances, Inventory Financials, Fixed Assets, Migrations, GST Doc Integration). Most of the new V10 entries in this specification are in Finance Management. / 2. Setup masters are the next gap. Many Sales, Product and Sourcing codes are not in the V10 mock and are proposed as new entries under the relevant Setups sub-menu. / 3. Several transaction screens are missing from V10, including Process Definition, Good Transfer Note, Alteration / Additional Process, Liability Management, Chargebacks, Supplier Block Booking, Advance License, Sample Value Confirmation, Return-to-Processor and Return-to-Supplier dispatch, OC to OC Roll Transfer and Update Pallet Location. / 4. V10 adds 86 menus that Shahi does not have today (for example Supplier Onboarding, Audits, Recipes, Batch Traceability, Security & Access, Workflow & Approvals). Seven of them are marked "Removed in V10" and are excluded. / 5. Many legacy menu rows are actions, not screens. Legacy entries named New, List, Search or Pending normally become buttons or tabs inside the parent page (see 6.3).
- validation (§ 3. Menu standards): Every entry in the V10 menu must follow these rules.
- definition (§ 3. Menu standards): They were applied to the Proposed Menu column and are the acceptance rules for any later change.
- definition (§ 3. Menu standards): A path is Module > Sub Menu > Page Name.
- definition (§ 3. Menu standards): The page name is the last level of the path.
- validation (§ 3. Menu standards): Column K must always equal the last part of column J.
- validation (§ 3. Menu standards): The page title shown on screen must use the same text.
- definition (§ 3. Menu standards): A page that lists records is named in the plural (Suppliers, Seasons, Themes, Production Orders, PO Templates).
- definition (§ 3. Menu standards): Where the legacy name is plural, the V10 name must not be singular.
- validation (§ 3. Menu standards): Where the legacy name is plural, the V10 name must not be singular.
- definition (§ 3. Menu standards): Levels are separated by space, greater-than sign, space (" > ").
- validation (§ 3. Menu standards): Two different screens must not share the same full path.
- validation (§ 3. Menu standards): Where they do, one must be renamed (see 8.2).
- definition (§ 3. Menu standards): Actions are not menu items.
- validation (§ 3. Menu standards): Rows such as "Yudesh Sir" or requirement notes typed as menu rows must not be built.
- workflow_steps (§ 3. Menu standards): 3. Menu standards: / 1. Three levels at most. A path is Module > Sub Menu > Page Name. Where the legacy structure was deeper, the levels in between are dropped and the page sits directly under the sub-menu. / 2. The page name is the last level of the path. Column K must always equal the last part of column J. The page title shown on screen must use the same text. / 3. List menus use the plural. A page that lists records is named in the plural (Suppliers, Seasons, Themes, Production Orders, PO Templates). Where the legacy name is plural, the V10 name must not be singular. / 4. Separator format. Levels are separated by space, greater-than sign, space (" > "). No empty levels, no double spaces, no missing spaces. / 5. Title case. Every word in a menu label starts with a capital letter except short joining words (of, for, to, and). Example: Payment Terms, not Payment terms. / 6. One path, one page. Two different screens must not share the same full path. Where they do, one must be renamed (see 8.2). / 7. Actions are not menu items. New, List, Search, Pending and similar entries become buttons or tabs inside the page and are controlled by action-level permissions. / 8. No test, personal or note rows. Rows such as "Yudesh Sir" or requirement notes typed as menu rows must not be built.

- validation (§ 6. Development specification › 6.1 Menu configuration record): The record must hold the fields below.
- table (§ 6. Development specification › 6.1 Menu configuration record, table 19): Table 19: Field, Description, Source (11 rows; identifiers: Field)
- validation (§ 6. Development specification › 6.2 Navigation behaviour): The menu must never show more than three levels.
- validation (§ 6. Development specification › 6.2 Navigation behaviour): Menu search, where available, must index the Page Name and the legacy names in the Legacy menu IDs field, so users can still find a page by its old name during the transition.
- workflow_steps (§ 6. Development specification › 6.2 Navigation behaviour): 6.2 Navigation behaviour: / 1. The menu must never show more than three levels. A Level 2 item opens its list of pages; it does not open a page itself. / 2. The breadcrumb on every page reads Module > Sub Menu > Page Name, using exactly the text in the build list. / 3. The browser tab title and the page heading use the Page Name. / 4. A V10 path that appears under more than one legacy module (for example Reporting, or Sales > Setups > Payment Terms reached from Sourcing and Finance) is built once and shown once. / 5. Menu search, where available, must index the Page Name and the legacy names in the Legacy menu IDs field, so users can still find a page by its old name during the transition.
- validation (§ 6. Development specification › 6.3 Actions inside pages): Dev must not create these as menu items.
- workflow_steps (§ 6. Development specification › 6.3 Actions inside pages): 6.3 Actions inside pages: / 1. List and Search become the default view of the page (a list with search/filter). / 2. New becomes a button on the list view that opens the entry form. / 3. Other children with their own screen (for example Supplier Invoice Return List, Download Invoices, Update GL Date) keep their own V10 path as shown in Section 5. / 4. Each action has its own permission key under the page Menu ID (for example FINANCE.AP.SUPPLIERINVOICE.NEW), so that rights held on the legacy New or List entries can be carried over exactly.
- validation (§ 6. Development specification › 6.4 Technology handling): The menu must open the page in the correct way for that technology.
- table (§ 6. Development specification › 6.4 Technology handling, table 20): Table 20: Technology, Pages (distinct V10 paths), Requirement (6 rows; identifiers: Technology)
- validation (§ 6. Development specification › 6.5 New menu entries): For each one Dev must create the menu record, link it to the existing legacy page (most new entries are existing Shahi screens that the V10 mock does not show yet) and apply the standards in Section 3.
- definition (§ 6. Development specification › 6.5 New menu entries): The largest blocks are Finance Management (141), Sales (30), Sourcing (25) and Products (23).
- validation (§ 6. Development specification › 6.5 New menu entries): The largest blocks are Finance Management (141), Sales (30), Sourcing (25) and Products (23).
- validation (§ 6. Development specification › 6.6 Legacy links and redirects): Saved bookmarks, dashboard tiles, e-mail links and notifications that point to a legacy menu must keep working.
- workflow_steps (§ 6. Development specification › 6.6 Legacy links and redirects): 6.6 Legacy links and redirects: / 1. Saved bookmarks, dashboard tiles, e-mail links and notifications that point to a legacy menu must keep working. Each legacy menu ID in Appendix A redirects to its V10 page. / 2. Where a legacy entry has become an action (New, List), the redirect opens the V10 page with that action selected. / 3. Legacy entries excluded from V10 (Section 8.4) redirect to the module home page with a short message.
- validation (§ 6. Development specification › 6.7 Permissions): A user sees a Page only if they hold its view permission.
- definition (§ 6. Development specification › 6.7 Permissions): A Menu group is shown only if the user can see at least one page under it.
- validation (§ 6. Development specification › 6.7 Permissions): A Menu group is shown only if the user can see at least one page under it.
- validation (§ 6. Development specification › 6.7 Permissions): Dev must produce a migration report listing every user and role whose visible menu changes, for Implementation to review (7.1).
- workflow_steps (§ 6. Development specification › 6.7 Permissions): 6.7 Permissions: / 1. A user sees a Page only if they hold its view permission. A Menu group is shown only if the user can see at least one page under it. An empty module is hidden. / 2. Rights migrate from legacy menu IDs to V10 Menu IDs using Appendix A. Where several legacy entries merge into one V10 page, the user gets the page if they had any of the legacy entries; action rights are carried per action. / 3. Dev must produce a migration report listing every user and role whose visible menu changes, for Implementation to review (7.1).
- workflow_steps (§ 6. Development specification › 6.8 Acceptance criteria): 6.8 Acceptance criteria: / 1. Every Page in Section 5 can be reached in no more than three clicks from the main menu. / 2. No menu path has more than three levels and no two pages share a path. / 3. Menu label, page title and breadcrumb match the build list exactly, including plural and capitalisation. / 4. No New, List or Search entries appear as menu items; they are available as actions with working permissions. / 5. Every legacy menu ID in Appendix A opens the correct V10 page. / 6. A user migrated from a legacy role sees the same set of screens and actions as before, apart from changes approved in Section 8. / 7. All items marked Confirm or Folder (review) have a recorded decision before release.
- workflow_steps (§ 7. Implementation specification › 7.1 Roles and rights migration): 7.1 Roles and rights migration: / 1. Export the current Shahi roles, users and their menu rights before the change. / 2. Run the Dev migration (6.7) on a copy of production data. / 3. Compare the before and after menu for each role using the Dev migration report. Investigate every role that loses or gains a screen. / 4. Pay special attention to merged pages (Appendix A rows that share a V10 path) and to the Finance module, where most entries are new. / 5. Get sign-off on the final role matrix from the customer process owners for each module.
- workflow_steps (§ 7. Implementation specification › 7.2 User communication): 7.2 User communication: / 1. Publish a "Where did my menu go?" guide built from Appendix A, one page per legacy module, sorted by legacy menu name. / 2. Explain the three main changes: menus renamed (for example Buyer to Customer), menus moved between modules (for example Sales ASN to Logistic, Material Requisitions to Sourcing), and New/List entries now being buttons inside the page. / 3. Communicate module renames: Product → Products and Development, Production → Manufacturing, QC → Quality & Compliance, FA → Finance Management, Planning → Plan, TNA → Utilities > TNA, Admin → Administrators and Utilities.
- table (§ 7. Implementation specification › 7.3 Training, table 21): Table 21: Audience, Focus, Priority (6 rows; identifiers: Audience)
- workflow_steps (§ 7. Implementation specification › 7.4 User acceptance testing): 7.4 User acceptance testing: / 1. For each module, a key user opens every Page in Section 5 from the menu and confirms the right screen opens. / 2. Test at least one legacy bookmark or link per module and confirm the redirect. / 3. Test New, List and Search actions on merged pages with a user who had only one of the legacy rights. / 4. Confirm role visibility for at least one user per role in the migration report. / 5. Record defects against the Menu ID so Dev can trace them to the build list.
- workflow_steps (§ 7. Implementation specification › 7.5 Cut-over and rollback): 7.5 Cut-over and rollback: / 1. Freeze menu and role changes in Shahi from the agreed date until go-live. / 2. Deploy the V10 menu configuration and run the rights migration in the agreed downtime window. / 3. Smoke-test one page per module with a key user before releasing to all users. / 4. Keep the legacy menu configuration and role export so the previous menu can be restored if a blocking defect is found. / 5. Provide floor support for the first week, with the Appendix A guide at hand.
